Variants.Content: Geso is one of Iban's families, a life shaped by the whaling season and Cold Sea trade. Hunting a whale does not mean that wealth has been obtained: towing, cutting, refining, preserving, aggregate processing and loading all require a lot of coordination, and any link that is out of order can turn the harvest into corruption and fighting. The foundations of Geso thus existed between ship and shore, both to win the trust of those who dared to go to sea, and to discipline overseers, maintain workshops and arrange winter storage. Fleet size can change, the responsibilities around risk and allocation do not.

Whalers judge a Geso based on whether it is willing to use good ropes, a good fork and enough manpower, and whether it can honor its share after casualties. If a family only shares whale oil and does not share risks, it will soon be unable to hire experienced crew members.

The refiners and bonesmiths wanted Gesso to keep the harvest in order. Rushing to start a trade union will waste materials, and delaying payment of wages will make the most skilled workers go elsewhere.

When the family on the shore heard Gesso's name, they thought of the sailing list and the shadow of the ship that had not returned. For them, the glory is not the biggest whale bone, but someone remembering to knock on the widow's door in the winter.

Entry Gaeso The reputation of Iban's Cold Sea family is based on whaling, processing, ship supply, and responsibility for families in distress. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
